paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: the truth about Jesus can sit in plain sight and still get missed. Festus walked in expecting crimes. What he got were arguments about their own religion and "a certain Jesus who had died, but whom Paul affirmed to be alive" (Acts 25:19). Festus called Jesus "a certain Jesus," like a name on a stack of paperwork, and he never asked the one question that mattered, which was whether it was TRUE (Acts 25:19).

And look at what the whole room could see. Festus told them he "found he had done nothing worthy of death" (Acts 25:25), and he had nothing definite to write about Paul (Acts 25:26). The whole Jewish community was crying out that Paul "ought not to live any longer" (Acts 25:24), and still no charge held up. Paul stood there with a clean record and one message: Jesus is alive.

So what does that mean for you, baker? Faith in Jesus doesn't need a crowd cheering or a king clapping. Paul stood in a hall full of pomp, and the only thing he carried in was the truth about Jesus. Hold that truth steady like that, and let it stand on its own. This story isn't over, because Paul is about to speak.
